data.note:
Reflection: specimen was colchicine (CID 6167, ChEMBL Tubulin inhibitor). I called Microtubule stabilizers; truth is Microtubule destabilizers.

My error was overweighting the atlas NSC vote (2/4, decisive similarity 0.61 only at 3 uM) against the non-atlas evidence the PI flagged: tub_mean fell monotonically with dose (rho=-1.0, z=-5.1 at 3 uM), opposite to bundling/increased signal expected for stabilizers; microscopist saw intact/diffuse tubulin with no bundling at 1 and 3 uM; frac_mitotic_like was not dose-dependent. The extreme high-dose fragmentation (nuc_solidity z=-36) plus cell loss was non-discriminating cytotoxicity, not stabilizer-specific. I kept 0.35 on stabilizers as weak plurality when destabilizers fit the tubulin-loss trend better.

Literature confirms colchicine-site binding as destabilizing: colchicine-site binders as microtubule-destabilizing agents (PMID:35939994), agents binding the colchicine site of tubulin (PMID:28640209), colchicine-binding-site inhibitors on tubulin intersubunit interaction (PMID:37599936), and colchicine-site binder effects on microtubule organization (PMID:24530796). Lesson: when transition-dose replicates are near-noise and tubulin intensity trends oppose the atlas, downgrade the atlas and prioritize the tubulin-direction test.

reflection.text:
I correctly placed the compound on the microtubule-mitotic axis but got the direction wrong, calling a stabilizer for a colchicine-site destabilizer. I overweighted the early atlas vote (NSC 2/2, then 2/4) driven almost entirely by the single 3 uM well at similarity 0.61, while the 0.3-1.0 uM wells were near-noise at 0.19-0.27 voting for other classes.

The non-atlas data pointed away from stabilizers and I discounted it: tub_mean fell monotonically with dose (rho -1.0) with low tubulin at 1-3 uM, the microscopist saw no bundling at 3 uM and intact filamentous tubulin at 1 uM, and frac_mitotic_like was not dose-dependent (rho -0.20). I attributed the extreme high-dose nuclear fragmentation (nuc_solidity z -36.0) to stabilizer arrest instead of recognizing it as a catastrophic segregation-failure/cytotoxicity confound seen in both stabilizer and destabilizer classes.

The acquisition plan caused this: I spent all four wells as singletons across doses with no replicate, so the transition-dose contradiction at 1.0 uM (tub_mean z -2.7, visually intact tubulin) could not be resolved, leaving the requested 1.0 uM replicate 2 unacquired and the 0.6 confidence unjustified.
what_was_right: Recognized microtubule/mitotic-segregation axis from extreme nuclear shape defect (nuc_solidity z -36.0, nuc_form_factor z -13.2) and microscopist mitotic candidates
Captured dose-dependent cell loss (cell_count rho -1.0) and rising multinucleate proxy (rho +1.0) consistent with tubulin-inhibition segregation failure
Late downgrade to 0.35 correctly registered that atlas support was only a weak 2/4 plurality with low transition-dose similarities
what_was_wrong: Called Microtubule stabilizers despite tub_mean falling monotonically with dose (rho -1.0) and low tubulin signal at 1-3 uM, opposite to increased/bundled signal expected for stabilizers
Overweighted early NSC 2/2 vote that rested on the single 3 uM well (similarity 0.61) while 0.3-1.0 uM wells were near-noise (0.19-0.27) voting Kinase inhibitors and Actin disruptors
Discounted microscopist explicit no-bundling at 3 uM and DMSO-like intact tubulin at 1 uM plus non-dose-dependent frac_mitotic_like (rho -0.20) arguing against clean stabilizer arrest
Used four singleton doses with no replicate so high-dose fragmentation confound could not be separated and requested 1.0 uM replicate 2 transition test was impossible on zero budget

citations.claim: Colchicine-site binders act as microtubule-destabilizing agents.
Agents that bind the colchicine site of tubulin cause microtubule destabilization.
Colchicine-binding-site inhibitors disrupt tubulin intersubunit interactions.
Colchicine-site binding produces distinct effects on microtubule depolymerization and organization.
Microtubule-stabilizing agents promote polymerization and bundling, opposite to tubulin loss.

With every dose represented by one well and no replicate, the stated 0.6 is over-confident: stabilizers are at best a plurality, not more likely than all alternatives combined.

Requested: Acquire one well at dose index 6 (1.0 µM), replicate 2 - the highest sub-catastrophic dose, where the leading hypotheses make opposite, testable predictions before the 3 µM fragmentation/cell-loss confound. A stabilizer should reproducibly show preserved-to-increased tubulin signal/bundling with mitotic enrichment at this dose; the existing replicate-1 result instead gave weak, contradictory signals (tub_mean z=-2.7, frac_mitotic_like z=+2.4, visually intact tubulin, e7/e13). If replicate 2 reproduces tubulin loss without bundling/mitotic enrichment, the stabilizer call should fall toward Microtubule destabilizers or a mitotic-segregation class; if it shows bundling with mitotic enrichment, the top call gains its first non-atlas support. This single replicate directly tests the weak transition-dose effect on which discrimination depends.

## Reflection

I correctly placed the compound on the microtubule-mitotic axis but got the direction wrong, calling a stabilizer for a colchicine-site destabilizer. I overweighted the early atlas vote (NSC 2/2, then 2/4) driven almost entirely by the single 3 uM well at similarity 0.61, while the 0.3-1.0 uM wells were near-noise at 0.19-0.27 voting for other classes.

The non-atlas data pointed away from stabilizers and I discounted it: tub_mean fell monotonically with dose (rho -1.0) with low tubulin at 1-3 uM, the microscopist saw no bundling at 3 uM and intact filamentous tubulin at 1 uM, and frac_mitotic_like was not dose-dependent (rho -0.20). I attributed the extreme high-dose nuclear fragmentation (nuc_solidity z -36.0) to stabilizer arrest instead of recognizing it as a catastrophic segregation-failure/cytotoxicity confound seen in both stabilizer and destabilizer classes.

The acquisition plan caused this: I spent all four wells as singletons across doses with no replicate, so the transition-dose contradiction at 1.0 uM (tub_mean z -2.7, visually intact tubulin) could not be resolved, leaving the requested 1.0 uM replicate 2 unacquired and the 0.6 confidence unjustified.

What was right:
- Recognized microtubule/mitotic-segregation axis from extreme nuclear shape defect (nuc_solidity z -36.0, nuc_form_factor z -13.2) and microscopist mitotic candidates
- Captured dose-dependent cell loss (cell_count rho -1.0) and rising multinucleate proxy (rho +1.0) consistent with tubulin-inhibition segregation failure
- Late downgrade to 0.35 correctly registered that atlas support was only a weak 2/4 plurality with low transition-dose similarities

What was wrong or missed:
- Called Microtubule stabilizers despite tub_mean falling monotonically with dose (rho -1.0) and low tubulin signal at 1-3 uM, opposite to increased/bundled signal expected for stabilizers
- Overweighted early NSC 2/2 vote that rested on the single 3 uM well (similarity 0.61) while 0.3-1.0 uM wells were near-noise (0.19-0.27) voting Kinase inhibitors and Actin disruptors
- Discounted microscopist explicit no-bundling at 3 uM and DMSO-like intact tubulin at 1 uM plus non-dose-dependent frac_mitotic_like (rho -0.20) arguing against clean stabilizer arrest
- Used four singleton doses with no replicate so high-dose fragmentation confound could not be separated and requested 1.0 uM replicate 2 transition test was impossible on zero budget

Proposed next experiment: Fixed-cell high-resolution anti-tubulin plus phospho-H3/DNA spindle imaging across 0.1-3 uM versus paclitaxel stabilizer and nocodazole/colchicine destabilizer controls to quantify tubulin polymer mass, bundling versus depolymerization, mitotic index and multinucleation.
